About the Position

This project explores how to embed intelligence directly into the 'body' of robotic materials, sitting at the intersection of mechanical metamaterials, robotics, active matter physics, and embodied AI.

OpportunityFully Funded PhD Studentship: Embodying Intelligence in Robotic Materials
HostUniversity of Birmingham
LocationBirmingham, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingFully Funded
Stipend£21,805 per year (UKRI rate for 2026/27)
Application Deadline6 November 2026
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Basic Information

  • Full Project Title: Embodying Intelligence in Robotic Materials
  • Host Institution: University of Birmingham
  • Department: School of Engineering (Mechanical Engineering)
  • Supervisor: Dr Jack Binysh
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Duration: 42 months
  • Start Date: Autumn 2026 or January 2027
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (Home UK students)
  • Stipend: £21,805 per year (UKRI rate for 2026/27)
  • Tuition Fees: Covered for Home students
  • Eligibility: UK Home students (strong international applicants encouraged to contact supervisor)
  • Application Deadline: 6 November 2026
  • IELTS Requirement: 6.0 (no component below 5.5)
  • Contact: j.binysh@bham.ac.uk

Project Description

This project explores how to embed intelligence directly into the "body" of robotic materials, rather than relying solely on a central processor. The research sits at the intersection of mechanical metamaterials, robotics, active matter physics, and embodied AI. You will investigate self-learning active mechanical networks through a combination of tabletop experiments and theoretical modelling. Specific research will focus on developing decentralised learning techniques, capturing the non-linear dynamics of networks, exploring the relationship between network structure and function, and designing and executing tabletop robotic experiments.

Requirements

  • Excellent undergraduate/Master's degree in Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field
  • Fluency in spoken and written English

Contact

  • Email: j.binysh@bham.ac.uk

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/research/centres-institutes/research-in-mechanical-engineering/mechanical-engineering-phd-opportunities

Source: birmingham.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 6 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

About University of Birmingham

The University of Birmingham is a public research university in Birmingham, England, and a Russell Group member. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral study across engineering, medicine, science, business, humanities and social sciences. Research and teaching bring together different disciplines to investigate challenges affecting health, technology, communities and the environment.

Official website: https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/

How to Apply

Submit your application via the Mechanical Engineering PhD portal, specifying the project title and supervisor (Jack Binysh).
